reports-certificate-health (files/sysmon/check_puppet_cert_health.py:11): the script runs 'puppet certregen healthcheck --all --render-as yaml' as root and prints OK/Warning/Critical lines with exit 0/1/2 (lines 29-48); the expect matches that Nagios form. mismatch refuses-to-run-unprivileged: varies only the account (runuser -u nobody dropped -> root), which by lines 12-21 must change the verdict from 'please run as root'. In my run it printed the certregen failure instead, so it failed as required

finding reports-certificate-health: expected '(OK|Warning|Critical): ...\nrc=[012]', saw "command 'puppet certregen healthcheck --all --render-as yaml' failed\nrc=1". I confirmed by hand that 'puppet certregen' is 'Unknown subcommand' on puppet8node (puppet 8.24.2) and on the lab master puppet8master (openvox 8.24.2, whose production modules hold no certregen module); the upstream baseline cf477c6 references certregen only in the script itself

purpose covered: Purpose (a Nagios check on the Puppet master, run by naemon via sudo, reporting the earliest certificate expiry with 10/30-day thresholds) matches the whole baseline manifest (package, script file, sudo::conf) and the script. Tested: script and python3-yaml installed, naemon sudo rule present and sudoers valid, the check refuses unprivileged runs (with a mismatch), and a root run produces a Nagios report (a finding: certregen is absent on OpenVox 8). Uncovered: the expired/10/30-day thresholds. That is honest: the script's only data source, 'puppet certregen healthcheck', is an unknown subcommand on OpenVox 8, which I verified by hand on the agent node and on the lab master (also a server role). So no lab node can reach the thresholds until the finding is resolved, and the capability lift names that. Note: the reporting check runs on the agent node, not on the active puppetserver node (p8lab-puppetserver was powered off, so I could not check it by hand). The same failure on puppet8master shows a master role would not change the outcome.
